learning_outcomes.text: Have systematic knowledge and understanding of the key concepts and aspects of hydraulic systems and machines.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve problems of hydraulic systems and machines using established methods.
Be able to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods in hydraulic systems and machines.
Have an understanding of different methods in fluid mechanics and the ability to use them.
Be able to combine theory and practice to solve fluid mechanics problems.
Have an understanding of applicable methods and techniques in fluid mechanics systems and machines and their limitations.
Function effectively both individually and in a team.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their branch of engineering.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory skills.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
Understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and problem solving within their area of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering, to meet the required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid mechanical systems and machines.

syllabus_topics: Steady flow of liquids in conduits.
Distributed head losses. Colebrook correlation and Moody diagram.
Non-circular section conduits. Hydraulic diameter.
Head loss in singular elements: valves, elbows, bends, expansions, contractions, etc.
Coupling of turbomachinery to a hydraulic installation.
Steady flow of liquids in piping systems.
Conduits in series and in parallel.
Analysis of branched networks: three-reservoir problem.
Analysis of meshed networks. Matrix algorithm for solving meshed networks and its numerical implementation.
Transient phenomena in conduits.
Theory of incompressible transients in conduits.
Characteristic acceleration and transfer times. Quasi-steady limit.
Estimation of characteristic magnitudes of unsteady flow in conduit systems. Non-dimensionalization of equations.
Practical application examples. Surge tank.
Compressibility effects. Basic water hammer theory. Transmission and reflection of water hammer waves. Practical application examples.
Introduction to turbomachinery.
Generalities. Classification of incompressible fluid machines.
Real characteristic curves of pumps and turbines.
Cavitation in turbomachinery.
Similarity in turbomachinery.
Coupling of pumps and turbines to the hydraulic network.
teaching_methods: Lectures, where the knowledge students must acquire will be presented.
Solving exercises by the student that will help them self-evaluate their knowledge and acquire the necessary skills.
Numerical calculation practicals in computer lab and report writing.
assessment_rules: Continuous assessment (EC) is 0.2*TC + 0.4*EP1 + 0.4*EP2; if EC>=5 and EP1, EP2>=4, the course is passed. Otherwise, the final grade (NF) for the ordinary call is NF=0.2*TC+0.15*EP1+0.15*EP2+0.5*EFO, where EFO=0.5*MAX(EP1,EFO1)+0.5*MAX(EP2,EFO2) and EFO1, EFO2 must be >=4 to pass the EFO. The extraordinary call uses NF=MAX(0.2*TC+0.8*EFE,EFE). A final grade of NF>=5 is required to pass the course.
